referees.quote: Overall, I recommend publication after the following questions are addressed.
The data are extensive, mutually supportive, and the conclusions are largely solid... several points need clarification or improvement before publication.
It could be suitable for publication in Nature Communications after the authors address the following points... Additional measurements over a broader Δτ range would strengthen this claim

note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; the first round is Version 0 of this file. None of the referees used the scale terms, so all three levels are inferred. R1 asked only for clarifications, a figure fix, a twist-angle comment and code availability, so minor. R2 called the conclusions 'largely solid' and asked mainly for explanations, a re-analysis of existing low-density data and figure changes, so minor. R3 is borderline between minor and major. The tone is positive ('high potential significance'), but R3 asks for more direct or independent evidence for the central IX2 assignment, evidence of charge neutrality and new measurements over a broader delay range. That is substantial new data and analysis, so major. R1 did not take part in round 2, where R2 and R3 recommended publication.
